newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ lamb export earnings rise 15 pct in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: NZ lamb export earnings rise 15 pct in 1995/96.

text.p: Surging global demand for sheepmeat saw New Zealand lamb export earnings rise 15 percent to NZ$1.23 billion in the 1995/96 season, Meat Board chairman John Acland said on Tuesday.

Acland said the result underscored the positive global outlook for New Zealand's sheepmeat industry, which is using further processing to differentiate New Zealand lamb from its red meat competitors who trade largely on a commodity basis.
"Sheep farmers can be optimistic about lamb returns for the 1996/97 season and beyond," he said.
Acland said increased access into high-value European Union markets had been secured for New Zealand's sheepmeat during the Gatt Uruguay Round.

Returns had also improved because more lamb was being further processed in New Zealand than ever before. Over 70 percent of New Zealand lamb was exported in further processed form in 1995/96, compared to 40 percent 10 years ago.
Acland said more consumers had turned to New Zealand lamb as a safe food in the wake of the BSE or "mad cow" crisis in Europe.

Exports to the European Union accounted for 56 percent of volume in 1995/96, but returned 66 percent of total lamb export dollars. The total value of lamb exports to the United States rose 27 percent, while volume rose 12 percent.
Acland said New Zealand's lamb trade with the Middle East had recovered after a difficult year in 1994/95, returning NZ$117 million in 1995/96.
